study_overview:
Brief Summary

            This is a Phase 1/2, multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of single and multiple doses of DNL593 in two parts followed by an optional open-label extension (OLE) period.

            Part A will evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK, and PD of single doses of DNL593 in healthy male and healthy female participants of nonchildbearing potential. Part B will evaluate the safety, tolerability, PK, and PD of multiple doses of DNL593 in participants with frontotemporal dementia (FTD) over 25 weeks. Part B will be followed by Part C, an optional 18-month OLE period available for all participants who complete Part B.
            Official Title
            A Phase 1/2, Multicenter, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double Blind Single Dose and Multiple Dose Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of DNL593 in Healthy Participants and Participants With Frontotemporal Dementia Followed by an Open-Label Extension
            Conditions
            Frontotemporal Dementia
            Intervention / Treatment

                Drug: DNL593
                Drug: Placebo

            Sponsor: Denali Therapeutics

emails.subject: URGENT: Significant Protocol Deviation - Study FTD-202 - Site 101 - Participant 101-008
emails.body:
Hi Kevin,

Please be advised of a significant protocol deviation for participant 101-008 in the FTD-202 study.

The participant missed their scheduled Week 12 visit today (May 15, 2023), which was a dosing visit for Part B of the study. All associated safety assessments, including blood draws and vital signs, were also missed.

The participant's caregiver called this morning to inform us of a family emergency that prevented them from attending. They were unable to provide a timeline for rescheduling at that moment.

We have documented this in the source and have attached the initial protocol deviation form. Please provide guidance on the following:
1. The window for rescheduling the visit and administering the dose.
2. How to handle the missed safety assessments.
3. Any additional documentation required beyond the standard PD form.

Thank you for your urgent attention to this matter.

Best regards,

Sarah Jones
Study Coordinator
Southview Research Center
(555) 123-4567

emails.subject: Re: URGENT: Significant Protocol Deviation - Study FTD-202 - Site 101 - Participant 101-008
emails.body:

Following up as promised. I have discussed this case with Dr. Volkov. Please proceed with the following guidance:

1.  **Rescheduling:** Reschedule the participant for the Week 12 visit as soon as possible. The visit must occur within 72 hours of the original appointment time. Please prioritize all safety assessments upon their arrival.
2.  **Dosing:** The missed dose of the investigational product should be administered at this rescheduled visit, provided all safety assessments are within acceptable limits and the PI confirms it is safe to do so.
3.  **Documentation:** Please ensure this is fully documented as a significant protocol deviation in the eCRF and source. Detail the reason for the missed visit and all actions taken. Update the protocol deviation form with the resolution and upload it to the TMF.

emails.subject: Query - Protocol XYZ123 - Site 101 - Unblinding & Transition to Part C
emails.body:
Hi David,

Hope you are having a good week.

We have a patient (101-004) who is approaching their final visit in the double-blind Part B of the study. We are preparing for their potential transition to the open-label extension (Part C) and would appreciate some clarification on the specific procedures.

Could you please provide a step-by-step guide or point us to the exact section in the protocol/pharmacy manual that details the unblinding process within the IXRS system? We want to ensure we follow the correct procedure for unblinding the patient's Part B treatment assignment and transitioning them to the open-label drug supply for Part C.

Any specific guidance on documentation requirements for this transition would also be very helpful.

Thank you for your support.

Best regards,

Sarah Jenkins, CCRC
Clinical Research Coordinator
University Health Center
Site 101

emails.subject: RE: Query - Protocol XYZ123 - Site 101 - Unblinding & Transition to Part C
emails.body:
Hi Sarah,

Thanks for reaching out and for your proactive planning. This is an important process to get right.

The detailed procedures for unblinding and transitioning to Part C are outlined in Protocol v4.0, Section 8.5. I have also attached a quick reference guide that our team created which summarizes the IXRS steps.

In short, the process is as follows:
1.  Confirm all Part B end-of-treatment assessments are complete and the patient has consented for Part C.
2.  The designated unblinded site staff (e.g., Pharmacist) must log into the IXRS.
3.  Navigate to the 'Unblinding' module for patient 101-004.
4.  Follow the on-screen prompts to confirm the unblinding request. The system will then reveal the treatment assignment from Part B.
5.  This event must be documented on the Unblinding Log and in the patient's source notes.
6.  Once unblinded, you can then proceed with the 'Transition to Open-Label' workflow in IXRS to have the first Part C drug kit assigned.

Please ensure the eCRF is updated accordingly to reflect the completion of Part B and the start of Part C.

Let me know if you have any further questions after reviewing the attached guide.

Best,

David Chen
Clinical Research Associate
Innovate Pharma

emails.subject: RE: Query - Protocol XYZ123 - Site 101 - Unblinding & Transition to Part C
emails.body:
Hi David,

This is perfect. Thank you so much for the clear explanation and for providing the reference guide. This is exactly what we needed.

We will review the materials thoroughly and proceed as instructed for the patient's upcoming visit.

Best regards,

Sarah Jenkins, CCRC
Clinical Research Coordinator
University Health Center
Site 101

emails.subject: Study INP-FTD-201 - Part B Screening at Site 101 - Maplewood Clinical Research
emails.body:
Dear Dr. Grant and Brenda,

I hope this email finds you well.

First, I want to reiterate our appreciation for your team's outstanding recruitment efforts in Part A of the INP-FTD-201 study. Maplewood has consistently been one of our top-performing sites, and we are very grateful for your hard work.

As we've transitioned into Part B, I've been reviewing the weekly screening logs and noticed a significant drop-off in potential subjects being screened at your site over the past three weeks. 

We know that Part B has more specific criteria, but given your past success, I wanted to reach out proactively to see if you've encountered any specific barriers or challenges. Are you seeing fewer potential FTD patients, or are there other factors at play?

I would be happy to schedule a brief call next week to discuss this further and brainstorm any strategies or resources we at InnovatePharma could provide to support your recruitment efforts. Please let me know what day and time might work for you and the team.

Thank you again for your continued partnership.

Best regards,

Sarah Jones
Clinical Research Associate
InnovatePharma
sarah.jones@innovatepharma.com

emails.subject: RE: Study INP-FTD-201 - Part B Screening at Site 101 - Maplewood Clinical Research
emails.body:
Hi Sarah,

Thank you for reaching out and for your kind words about our work on Part A.

We have also noted the slowdown in screening for Part B and appreciate you contacting us. Dr. Grant and I were just discussing this yesterday. We believe it's a combination of a few factors. The exclusion criteria for Part B are proving to be quite restrictive for our local patient population, particularly the comorbidity requirements. Additionally, a new observational FTD study just opened at University Hospital across town, and it seems to be drawing from the same patient referral network.

We would welcome a call to discuss this. We want to get back on track. Would you be available next Tuesday, October 31st, in the morning? Anytime between 9 AM and 11 AM ET would work for us.

Best,

Brenda Starr
Study Coordinator
Maplewood Clinical Research
b.starr@maplewoodresearch.org

emails.subject: RE: Study INP-FTD-201 - Part B Screening at Site 101 - Maplewood Clinical Research
emails.body:
Hi Brenda,

Thank you for the prompt and transparent reply. That context is very helpful, and we understand the challenges posed by competing studies and stringent criteria.

Next Tuesday at 10:00 AM ET works perfectly for me. I will send a calendar invitation shortly with a proposed agenda, which will include discussing potential community outreach and reviewing the pre-screening checklist to help identify eligible patients more efficiently.

We are confident that by working together, we can find effective solutions.

Best regards,

Sarah Jones

emails.subject: URGENT Query: DNL593 Study - IP Accountability Discrepancy at Site 701
emails.body:
Hi Samantha,

Hope you are well.

During our routine monthly investigational product (IP) accountability check for the DNL593 study today, we identified a discrepancy.

Our physical count shows 14 vials of DNL593 (active drug), but our accountability logs indicate we should have 15 vials on hand. The placebo count is accurate. We have double-checked all dispensing records, patient visit logs, and destruction records from the past month and cannot account for the missing vial.

Attached is a scanned copy of our most recent accountability log for your review.

Please advise on the immediate next steps and any required documentation we need to complete on our end.

Best regards,

Dr. Alan Turing, RPh
Lead Pharmacist
University Health Research Center
Site 701

emails.subject: Re: URGENT Query: DNL593 Study - IP Accountability Discrepancy at Site 701
emails.body:

As a first step, please quarantine all remaining DNL593 and placebo stock for this study until we have a resolution. Please do not dispense any further IP.

Could you please also prepare a brief deviation note in the site file detailing the discovery of this discrepancy? I will follow up by the end of the day with a formal IP Discrepancy Form for you to complete and any further instructions from the team.

We will work with you to resolve this as quickly as possible.

Best,

Samantha Carter
Clinical Research Associate
PharmaTech Inc.

emails.subject: [URGENT] Study DTX-123: Repeated PK Sample Rejection - Site 101
emails.body:
Hi Jane,

I hope you are well.

I'm writing to report another issue with a PK sample being rejected by the central lab. This is for patient 101-005, and it's the third time this has happened in the last two months. The reason cited is again 'Improperly Processed - Insufficient Plasma Volume'.

We believe we are following the lab manual protocol precisely, specifically section 4.2 regarding centrifugation and aliquoting. We are concerned this may impact the patient's data integrity and are unsure how to proceed to prevent this from happening again.

Could you please provide some clarification or guidance on the processing steps? Perhaps there is a nuance we are missing.

I have attached the latest rejection notification from LabCorp for your reference.

Best regards,

Sarah Jones, CRC
Clinical Research Coordinator
University Hospital
Oncology Department

emails.subject: Re: [URGENT] Study DTX-123: Repeated PK Sample Rejection - Site 101
